full_judgment:
2. This Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal is directed against the Judgment and Order dated 03.08.2003 passed by the High Court Division in Criminal Misc. Case No.915 of 2000 discharging the rule and affirming the Judgment and Order dated 03.10.1999. passed by the learned Judge of the Special Tribunal No.2 and Additional Sessions Judge, Satkhira in Special Tribunal Case No.105 of 1989 convicting the petitioner under Section .5 of the Cruelty to Women (Deterrent Punishment) Ordinance, 1983 and sentencing him to suffer imprisonment for life and to pay a fine of Tk.1,00,000/- in default to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 5(five) years more. 

 3. In short, the case of the prosecution is as follows: 

 4. During the course of investigation both the accused persons made inculpatory confessional statements and the statement of the victim Joshua Begum was also recorded to corroborate the case of the prosecution narrated in the FIR. Besides the inculpatory confessional statement of the accused petitioner, victim's statement also established the case of the prosecution beyond any reasonable doubt and ultimately trial Court found the accused-petitioner guilty of the offence punishable under Section 5 of the Cruelty to Women (Deterrent Punishment) Ordinance, 1983 and awarded sentence to suffer imprisonment for life with fine of Tk.1.00,000/- in default to pay 5(five) years rigorous imprisonment more. 

 5. During the course of the trial the accused-petitioner Monir Hossain Sawpan got the victim married and meanwhile they have also been blessed with three children subsequently convicted-accused-petitioner filed Criminal Misc. Case No.9I5 of 2000 under Section 561 A of the Code of Criminal Procedure but the Rule has been discharged by the High Court Division affirming the judgment of the trial Court. 

 7. Mr. Mohammod Hossain, learned Advocate for the convicted-accused-petitioner concedes that this Court is not a trier of facts and it is not its duty to review, evaluate and weigh the probative value of the evidence adduced before the trial Court but can easily reconsider the period of sentence prescribed by law on the basis of the subsequent situation followed by the occurrence. Since in the instant case the convicted accused-petitioner has already served out sentence of imprisonment for more than 14 years he should he release in order to save the children arising out of his marriage with the victim.
